beats.text: Be honest: does everyone online seem more popular than you?
If yes? You're right! They are more popular. And it's not about you.
Researchers analyzed almost six million Twitter users and four hundred seventy-six million tweets.
A typical user's followers had about ten times more followers. Ten times! And activity? Even worse.
Eighty-eight percent of users posted less than the people they follow.
Here's why: it's math! Popular accounts follow and get followed by tons of people. So they show up in everyone's network. Including yours.
So no, you're not boring! Your feed is just a room full of the most popular people.

sources: Hodas, Kooti & Lerman (2013), 'Friendship Paradox Redux: Your Friends Are More Interesting Than You', ICWSM 2013 (arXiv:1304.3480). Twitter, second half of 2009: 5.8 million users, 476 million tweets. Followers typically ~10x more popular (by follower count) than the user; 88% of users less active than a typical friend (99% excluding inactive accounts). Via BPS Research Digest (May 2013).
Friendship paradox: Feld (1991), American Journal of Sociology.
ask: DOES YOUR FEED FEEL LIKE THIS?
